entries.what: Esri World Imagery 2025-09-05 (z19, 0.271 m/px) for the 1997 reshaped boulder zone
entries.by: agent: Burkitts shape agent (queue item 9, cloud)
entries.detail: The natural basalt rock platform is visible (traced, 31,485 m2 in frame, LOW confidence) but the sub-zone where about 12 boulders (about 300 m3) were moved in 1997 cannot be identified in it, and no source locates it. Tide state of the image is unknown (the waterline edge could shift tens of metres) and the frame cuts the platform at its south end. Drawing the platform would present the stage as the reef, so the shape is hidden.
entries.might_work: Dated low-tide imagery (Esri Wayback 2014+, Google Earth Pro history: Lior G10), 1997-98 aerials, or an account from Redgard / Bargara Boardriders (E12)

entries.what: YouTube videos 'Diving Bargara, Burkitt's Reef Marine Park' (wuJ__7Js-cY) and 'Surfing at Bargara Beach, QLD' (O3bEn8029XQ), and their extracted frames
entries.by: agent: Burkitts media re-check; Lior's review 2026-09-25
entries.detail: Lior (2026-09-25) found that neither shows the artificial reef. The first is shore-dive footage at the Burkitts Reef Marine Park dive site (sandy / rocky bottom, hard coral bommies, fish) sharing the name; the second is generic Bargara Beach surf-tourism footage with no mention of Burkitts Reef. Frames wuJ__7Js-cY_0025 and _0205 were rejected (registry img-06, img-07, display false). The dive site's depth to about 9 m is therefore not used as seabed for the reef.

entries.detail: Only one mention in the five PDFs: Rendle (2016) thesis Table 2.1, p.41, one row 'Bargara 1997, Harvey [Hervey] Bay QLD, 300 m3, rock, A$10,000' (same facts as the card).
